verses.original: וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־ הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וַיָּ֣שֶׂם עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שָׂרֵ֥י אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י מֵאֽוֹת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yip̄·qōḏ dā·wiḏ ’eṯ- hā·‘ām ’ă·šer ’it·tōw way·yā·śem ‘ă·lê·hem śā·rê ’ă·lā·p̄îm wə·śā·rê mê·’ō·wṯ
verses.literal: Then David reviewed his troops - and appointed over them commanders of thousands and of hundreds . . .
verses.literalPt: Davi passou revista ao povo que tinha consigo e pôs sobre eles capitães de mil e capitães de cem.

verses.original: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח דָּוִ֜ד אֶת־ הָעָ֗ם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֤ית בְּיַד־ יוֹאָב֙ וְ֠הַשְּׁלִשִׁית בְּיַ֨ד אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָה֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב וְהַ֨שְּׁלִשִׁ֔ת בְּיַ֖ד אִתַּ֣י הַגִּתִּ֑יס וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ הָעָ֔ם יָצֹ֥א אֵצֵ֛א גַּם־ אֲנִ֖י עִמָּכֶֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·šal·laḥ dā·wiḏ ’eṯ- hā·‘ām haš·šə·li·šîṯ bə·yaḏ- yō·w·’āḇ wə·haš·šə·li·šîṯ bə·yaḏ ’ă·ḇî·šay ben- ṣə·rū·yāh ’ă·ḥî yō·w·’āḇ wə·haš·šə·li·šiṯ bə·yaḏ ’it·tay hag·git·tīs way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- hā·‘ām yā·ṣō ’ê·ṣê gam- ’ă·nî ‘im·mā·ḵem
verses.literal: He sent out the troops a third . . . under Joab a third . . . under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah and a third . . . under Ittai the Gittite And the king said to the troops I will surely march out . . . with you as well
verses.literalPt: Enviou Davi ao povo, um terço sob o mando de Joabe, outro terço sob o mando de Abisai, filho de Zeruia, irmão de Joabe, e o outro terço sob o mando de Itai, geteu. O rei disse ao povo: Também eu hei de sair convosco.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָעָ֜ם לֹ֣א תֵצֵ֗א כִּי֩ אִם־ נֹ֨ס נָנ֜וּס לֹא־ יָשִׂ֧ימוּ אֵלֵ֣ינוּ לֵ֗ב וְאִם־ יָמֻ֤תוּ חֶצְיֵ֙נוּ֙ לֹֽא־ יָשִׂ֤ימוּ אֵלֵ֙ינוּ֙ לֵ֔ב כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֥ה כָמֹ֖נוּ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה אֲלָפִ֑ים וְעַתָּ֣ה ט֔וֹב כִּי־ תִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֥נוּ מֵעִ֖יר לַעְזִיר׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer hā·‘ām lō ṯê·ṣê kî ’im- nōs nā·nūs lō- yā·śî·mū ’ê·lê·nū lêḇ wə·’im- yā·mu·ṯū ḥeṣ·yê·nū lō- yā·śî·mū ’ê·lê·nū lêḇ kî- ‘at·tāh ḵā·mō·nū ‘ă·śā·rāh ’ă·lā·p̄îm wə·‘at·tāh ṭō·wḇ kî- ṯih·yeh- lā·nū mê·‘îr laʿ·zīr
verses.literal: But the people pleaded You must not go out For if we have to flee . . . they will not care . . . about us Even if half of us die they will not care . . . But you are worth ten thousand of us It is better now if you support us from the city
verses.literalPt: Respondeu, porém, o povo: Não sairás, pois se, na verdade, fugirmos, eles não se importarão conosco; nem se importarão conosco se morrer a metade de nós; pois tu és igual a dez mil de nós. É melhor que fiques na cidade para dali nos socorreres.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ יִיטַ֥ב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם אֶעֱשֶׂ֑ה וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ יַ֣ד הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ יָֽצְא֔וּ לְמֵא֖וֹת וְלַאֲלָפִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ă·lê·hem ham·me·leḵ ’ă·šer- yî·ṭaḇ bə·‘ê·nê·ḵem ’e·‘ĕ·śeh way·ya·‘ă·mōḏ ham·me·leḵ ’el- yaḏ haš·ša·‘ar wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām yā·ṣə·’ū lə·mê·’ō·wṯ wə·la·’ă·lā·p̄îm
verses.literal: I will do whatever seems best to you the king replied So he stood beside . . . the gate while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands
verses.literalPt: Tornou-lhes o rei: O que vos parece bem, isso farei. O rei pôs-se ao lado da porta, e saiu todo o povo a centenas e milhares.

verses.original: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־ י֠וֹאָב וְאֶת־ אֲבִישַׁ֤י וְאֶת־ אִתַּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְאַט־ לִ֖י לַנַּ֣עַר לְאַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם שָׁמְע֗וּ בְּצַוֺּ֥ת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים עַל־ דְּבַ֥ר אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·ṣaw ham·me·leḵ ’eṯ- yō·w·’āḇ wə·’eṯ- ’ă·ḇî·šay wə·’eṯ- ’it·tay lê·mōr lə·’aṭ- lî lan·na·‘ar lə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām šā·mə·‘ū bə·ṣaw·wōṯ ham·me·leḵ ’eṯ- kāl- haś·śā·rîm ‘al- də·ḇar ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: Now the king had commanded Joab Abishai and Ittai . . . Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding . . . Absalom
verses.literalPt: O rei deu ordem a Joabe, a Abisai e a Itai, dizendo: Por amor de mim, tratai com brandura ao mancebo, a Absalão. Todo o povo ouviu quando o rei dava ordem a todos os capitães acerca de Absalão.

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הָעָ֛ם הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִקְרַ֣את יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתְּהִ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בְּיַ֥עַר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ṣê hā·‘ām haś·śā·ḏeh liq·raṯ yiś·rā·’êl wat·tə·hî ham·mil·ḥā·māh bə·ya·‘ar ’ep̄·rā·yim
verses.literal: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim
verses.literalPt: Assim, saiu o povo ao campo contra Israel; e deu-se a batalha no bosque de Efraim.

verses.original: וַיִּנָּ֤גְפוּ שָׁם֙ עַ֣ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַתְּהִי־ שָׁ֞ם הַמַּגֵּפָ֧ה גְדוֹלָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃
verses.transliteration: way·yin·nā·ḡə·p̄ū šām ‘am yiś·rā·’êl lip̄·nê ‘aḇ·ḏê ḏā·wiḏ wat·tə·hî- šām ham·mag·gê·p̄āh ḡə·ḏō·w·lāh bay·yō·wm ha·hū ‘eś·rîm ’ā·lep̄
verses.literal: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants and the slaughter was . . . great that day twenty thousand men
verses.literalPt: Ali, foi o povo de Israel derrotado diante dos servos de Davi, e, naquele dia, houve uma grande derrota, com a perda de vinte mil homens.

verses.original: וַתְּהִי־ שָׁ֧ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה נָפֹצֵית עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיֶּ֤רֶב הַיַּ֙עַר֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל בָּעָ֔ם מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָכְלָ֛ה הַחֶ֖רֶב בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tə·hî- šām ham·mil·ḥā·māh nå̄·p̄ō·ṣēṯ ‘al- pə·nê ḵāl hā·’ā·reṣ way·ye·reḇ hay·ya·‘ar le·’ĕ·ḵōl bā·‘ām mê·’ă·šer ’ā·ḵə·lāh ha·ḥe·reḇ bay·yō·wm ha·hū
verses.literal: The battle spread over . . . the whole countryside and that day the forest devoured more people than . . . the sword
verses.literalPt: Pois ali se estendeu a batalha por toda a região; e o bosque consumiu, naquele dia, mais gente do que a espada consumiu.

verses.original: וַיִּקָּרֵא֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וְאַבְשָׁל֞וֹם רֹכֵ֣ב עַל־ הַפֶּ֗רֶד וַיָּבֹ֣א הַפֶּ֡רֶד תַּ֣חַת שׂוֹבֶךְ֩ הָאֵלָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֜ה וַיֶּחֱזַ֧ק רֹאשׁ֣וֹ בָאֵלָ֗ה וַיֻּתַּן֙ בֵּ֤ין הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהַפֶּ֥רֶד אֲשֶׁר־ תַּחְתָּ֖יו עָבָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·qā·rê ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm lip̄·nê ‘aḇ·ḏê ḏā·wiḏ wə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm rō·ḵêḇ ‘al- hap·pe·reḏ way·yā·ḇō hap·pe·reḏ ta·ḥaṯ śō·w·ḇeḵ hā·’ê·lāh hag·gə·ḏō·w·lāh way·ye·ḥĕ·zaq rō·šōw ḇā·’ê·lāh way·yut·tan bên haš·šā·ma·yim ū·ḇên hā·’ā·reṣ wə·hap·pe·reḏ ’ă·šer- taḥ·tāw ‘ā·ḇār
verses.literal: Now Absalom . . . was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree The mule under him kept going so that he was suspended in midair . . . . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Absalão, indo montado na sua mula, encontrou-se com os servos de Davi; a mula entrou debaixo dos ramos espessos dum grande carvalho, e Absalão, preso pela cabeça ao carvalho, ficou pendurado entre o céu e a terra; e a mula em que ia montado passou adiante.

verses.original: וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְיוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה֙ רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם תָּל֖וּי בָּאֵלָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yar ’îš ’e·ḥāḏ way·yag·gêḏ lə·yō·w·’āḇ way·yō·mer hin·nêh rā·’î·ṯî ’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lōm tā·lui bā·’ê·lāh
verses.literal: When one of the men saw this he told Joab I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree
verses.literalPt: Vendo isso um homem, avisou a Joabe e disse: Eis que vi Absalão pendurado num carvalho.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב לָאִישׁ֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ וְהִנֵּ֣ה רָאִ֔יתָ וּמַדּ֛וּעַ לֹֽא־ הִכִּית֥וֹ שָׁ֖ם אָ֑רְצָה וְעָלַ֗י לָ֤תֶת לְךָ֙ עֲשָׂ֣רָה כֶ֔סֶף וַחֲגֹרָ֖ה אֶחָֽת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer yō·w·’āḇ lā·’îš ham·mag·gîḏ lōw wə·hin·nêh rā·’î·ṯā ū·mad·dū·a‘ lō- hik·kî·ṯōw šām ’ā·rə·ṣāh wə·‘ā·lay lā·ṯeṯ lə·ḵā ‘ă·śā·rāh ḵe·sep̄ wa·ḥă·ḡō·rāh ’e·ḥāṯ
verses.literal: You just saw him Joab - exclaimed Why did you not strike him to the ground . . . right there I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt
verses.literalPt: Respondeu Joabe ao homem que lhe dera a notícia: Pois que o viste, por que não o feriste ali, derrubando-o por terra? E eu te haveria dado dez siclos de prata e um cinto.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָאִישׁ֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב וְלֹא אָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁקֵ֤ל עַל־ כַּפַּי֙ אֶ֣לֶף כֶּ֔סֶף לֹֽא־ אֶשְׁלַ֥ח יָדִ֖י אֶל־ בֶּן־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י בְאָזְנֵ֜ינוּ צִוָּ֣ה הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֹ֠תְךָ וְאֶת־ אֲבִישַׁ֤י וְאֶת־ אִתַּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שִׁמְרוּ־ מִ֕י בַּנַּ֖עַר בְּאַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer hā·’îš ’el- yō·w·’āḇ wə·lō ’ā·nō·ḵî šō·qêl ‘al- kap·pay ’e·lep̄ ke·sep̄ lō- ’eš·laḥ yā·ḏî ’el- ben- ham·me·leḵ kî ḇə·’ā·zə·nê·nū ṣiw·wāh ham·me·leḵ ’ō·ṯə·ḵā wə·’eṯ- ’ă·ḇî·šay wə·’eṯ- ’it·tay lê·mōr šim·rū- mî ban·na·‘ar bə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: The man replied - Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands I would not raise my hand against the son of the king For we heard the king - command you and Abishai and Ittai . . . Protect the young man Absalom for my sake
verses.literalPt: Tornou o homem a Joabe: Ainda quando eu pudesse pesar nas minhas mãos mil siclos de prata, não estenderia eu a mão contra o filho do rei; porque nós ouvimos a ordem que o rei te deu a ti, a Abisai e a Itai, dizendo: Guardai-me o mancebo Absalão.

verses.original: אֽוֹ־ עָשִׂ֤יתִי בְנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁ֔קֶר וְכָל־ דָּבָ֖ר לֹא־ יִכָּחֵ֣ד מִן־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב מִנֶּֽגֶד׃
verses.transliteration: ’ōw- ‘ā·śî·ṯî ḇə·nap̄·šō še·qer wə·ḵāl dā·ḇār lō- yik·kā·ḥêḏ min- ham·me·leḵ wə·’at·tāh tiṯ·yaṣ·ṣêḇ min·ne·ḡeḏ
verses.literal: If I had jeopardized . . . . . . . . . my own life and nothing is hidden from the king you would have abandoned me
verses.literalPt: Se eu tivesse obrado falsamente contra a sua vida, nada teria sido oculto ao rei, e tu mesmo te esquivarias de mim.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֔ב לֹא־ כֵ֖ן אֹחִ֣ילָה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיִּקַּח֩ שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה שְׁבָטִ֜ים בְּכַפּ֗וֹ וַיִּתְקָעֵם֙ בְּלֵ֣ב אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם עוֹדֶ֥נּוּ חַ֖י בְּלֵ֥ב הָאֵלָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer yō·w·’āḇ lō- ḵên ’ō·ḥî·lāh lə·p̄ā·ne·ḵā way·yiq·qaḥ šə·lō·šāh šə·ḇā·ṭîm bə·ḵap·pōw way·yiṯ·qā·‘êm bə·lêḇ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ‘ō·w·ḏen·nū ḥay bə·lêḇ hā·’ê·lāh
verses.literal: But Joab declared I am not going to wait like this with you And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive . . . in the oak tree
verses.literalPt: Disse Joabe: Não posso demorar-me contigo. Tomou na mão três dardos e traspassou com eles o coração de Absalão, que ainda estava vivo no carvalho.

verses.original: וַיָּסֹ֙בּוּ֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה נְעָרִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י כְּלֵ֣י יוֹאָ֑ב וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם וַיְמִיתֻֽהוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·sōb·bū ‘ă·śā·rāh nə·‘ā·rîm nō·śə·’ê kə·lê yō·w·’āḇ way·yak·kū ’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm way·mî·ṯu·hū
verses.literal: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom struck him and killed him
verses.literalPt: Cercaram-no dez mancebos que levavam as armas de Joabe, e feriram a Absalão, e mataram-no.

verses.original: וַיִּתְקַ֤ע יוֹאָב֙ בַּשֹּׁפָ֔ר וַיָּ֣שָׁב הָעָ֔ם מִרְדֹ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ חָשַׂ֥ךְ יוֹאָ֖ב אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiṯ·qa‘ yō·w·’āḇ baš·šō·p̄ār way·yā·šāḇ hā·‘ām mir·ḏōp̄ ’a·ḥă·rê yiś·rā·’êl kî- ḥā·śaḵ yō·w·’āḇ ’eṯ- hā·‘ām
verses.literal: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn and the troops broke off their pursuit . . . of Israel because Joab had restrained them . . .
verses.literalPt: Joabe tocou a trombeta, e o povo voltou de perseguir a Israel, pois Joabe deteve ao povo.

verses.original: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם וַיַּשְׁלִ֨יכוּ אֹת֤וֹ בַיַּ֙עַר֙ אֶל־ הַפַּ֣חַת הַגָּד֔וֹל וַיַּצִּ֧בוּ עָלָ֛יו גַּל־ אֲבָנִ֖ים גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֑ד וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נָ֖סוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְאָהֳלוֹ׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·ḥū ’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm way·yaš·lî·ḵū ’ō·ṯōw ḇay·ya·‘ar ’el- hap·pa·ḥaṯ hag·gā·ḏō·wl way·yaṣ·ṣi·ḇū ‘ā·lāw gal- ’ă·ḇā·nîm gā·ḏō·wl mə·’ōḏ wə·ḵāl yiś·rā·’êl nā·sū ’îš lə·ʾå̄·ho·lō
verses.literal: They took Absalom cast him into a large pit in the forest and piled a huge . . . mound of stones over him Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled each to his home
verses.literalPt: Levaram a Absalão, e lançaram-no numa grande cova no bosque, e erigiram sobre ele um mui grande montão de pedras. Todo o Israel fugiu, cada um para a sua tenda.

verses.original: וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֣ם לָקַ֗ח וַיַּצֶּב־ ל֤וֹ בְחַיָּו אֶת־ מַצֶּ֙בֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעֵֽמֶק־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֤י אָמַר֙ אֵֽין־ לִ֣י בֵ֔ן בַּעֲב֖וּר הַזְכִּ֣יר שְׁמִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֤א לַמַּצֶּ֙בֶת֙ עַל־ שְׁמ֔וֹ וַיִּקָּ֤רֵא לָהּ֙ יַ֣ד אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·’aḇ·šā·lōm lā·qaḥ way·yaṣ·ṣeḇ- lōw ḇə·ḥay·yå̄w ’eṯ- maṣ·ṣe·ḇeṯ ’ă·šer bə·‘ê·meq- ham·me·leḵ kî ’ā·mar ’ên- lî ḇên ba·‘ă·ḇūr haz·kîr šə·mî way·yiq·rā lam·maṣ·ṣe·ḇeṯ ‘al- šə·mōw way·yiq·qā·rê lāh yaḏ ’aḇ·šā·lōm ‘aḏ hay·yō·wm haz·zeh
verses.literal: During his lifetime Absalom . . . had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley for he had said I have no . . . son to preserve the memory of my name So he gave the pillar . . . his name and to this day it is called . . . Absalom’s Monument
verses.literalPt: Ora, Absalão, quando ainda vivia, tinha feito levantar para si a coluna, que está no vale do Rei, porque disse: Eu não tenho filho que conserve a memória do meu nome. Deu o seu nome à coluna; até o dia de hoje, ela se chama o Monumento de Absalão.

verses.original: וַאֲחִימַ֤עַץ בֶּן־ צָדוֹק֙ אָמַ֔ר אָר֣וּצָה נָּ֔א וַאֲבַשְּׂרָ֖ה אֶת־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּי־ שְׁפָט֥וֹ יְהוָ֖ה מִיַּ֥ד אֹיְבָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: wa·’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ ben- ṣā·ḏō·wq ’ā·mar ’ā·rū·ṣāh nā wa·’ă·ḇaś·śə·rāh ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ kî- šə·p̄ā·ṭōw Yah·weh mî·yaḏ ’ō·yə·ḇāw
verses.literal: Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies
verses.literalPt: Disse Aimaás, filho de Zadoque: Deixa-me correr e dar notícia ao rei que Jeová o vingou dos seus inimigos.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יוֹאָ֗ב לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ בְּשֹׂרָ֤ה אַתָּה֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וּבִשַּׂרְתָּ֖ בְּי֣וֹם אַחֵ֑ר וְהַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ לֹ֣א תְבַשֵּׂ֔ר כִּֽי־ עַל בֶּן־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מֵֽת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lōw yō·w·’āḇ lō ’îš bə·śō·rāh ’at·tāh hay·yō·wm haz·zeh ū·ḇiś·śar·tā bə·yō·wm ’a·ḥêr wə·hay·yō·wm haz·zeh lō ṯə·ḇaś·śêr kî- ʿal ben- ham·me·leḵ mêṯ
verses.literal: But Joab replied You are not the man to take good news today . . . You may do it another day but you must not do so today . . . because . . . the king’s son is dead
verses.literalPt: E Joabe lhe disse: Tu não serás hoje o portador das novas, mas noutro dia as levarás; hoje, porém, não as levarás; porque é morto o filho do rei.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹאָב֙ לַכּוּשִׁ֔י לֵ֛ךְ הַגֵּ֥ד לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֑יתָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ כוּשִׁ֛י לְיוֹאָ֖ב וַיָּרֹֽץ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer yō·w·’āḇ lak·kū·šî lêḵ hag·gêḏ lam·me·leḵ ’ă·šer rā·’î·ṯāh way·yiš·ta·ḥū ḵū·šî lə·yō·w·’āḇ way·yā·rōṣ
verses.literal: So Joab said to a Cushite Go tell the king what you have seen The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running
verses.literalPt: Disse Joabe ao cuxita: Vai dizer ao rei o que viste. O cuxita fez uma reverência a Joabe e partiu a correr.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֜וֹד אֲחִימַ֤עַץ בֶּן־ צָדוֹק֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב וִ֣יהִי מָ֔ה אָרֻֽצָה־ נָּ֥א גַם־ אָ֖נִי אַחֲרֵ֣י הַכּוּשִׁ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב לָֽמָּה־ זֶּ֞ה אַתָּ֥ה רָץ֙ בְּנִ֔י וּלְכָ֖ה אֵין־ בְּשׂוֹרָ֥ה מֹצֵֽאת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·sep̄ ‘ō·wḏ ’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ ben- ṣā·ḏō·wq way·yō·mer ’el- yō·w·’āḇ wî·hî māh ’ā·ru·ṣāh- nā ḡam- ’ā·nî ’a·ḥă·rê hak·kū·šî way·yō·mer yō·w·’āḇ lām·māh- zeh ’at·tāh rāṣ bə·nî ū·lə·ḵāh ’ên- bə·śō·w·rāh mō·ṣêṯ
verses.literal: Ahimaaz son of Zadok however, persisted . . . and said to Joab . . . No matter what please let me also run behind the Cushite My son Joab replied why . . . do you want to run since you will not receive a reward
verses.literalPt: Então, tornou Aimaás, filho de Zadoque, a dizer a Joabe: Seja o que for, deixa-me também correr após o cuxita. Joabe disse: Por que queres correr, meu filho? Visto que não receberás recompensa pelas novas.

verses.original: וִיהִי־ מָ֣ה אָר֔וּץ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ ר֑וּץ וַיָּ֤רָץ אֲחִימַ֙עַץ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַכִּכָּ֔ר וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־ הַכּוּשִֽׁי׃
verses.transliteration: wî·hî- māh ’ā·rūṣ way·yō·mer lōw rūṣ way·yā·rāṣ ’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ de·reḵ hak·kik·kār way·ya·‘ă·ḇōr ’eṯ- hak·kū·šî
verses.literal: No matter what I want to run he replied Then run Joab told him So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite
verses.literalPt: Aconteça, porém, o que acontecer, hei de correr, respondeu Aimaás. Então, disse Joabe: Corre. Aimaás correu pelo caminho de Quicar e passou ao cuxita.

verses.original: וְדָוִ֥ד יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בֵּין־ שְׁנֵ֣י הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הַצֹּפֶ֜ה אֶל־ גַּ֤ג הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ אֶל־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וַיִּשָּׂ֤א אֶת־ עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה־ אִ֖ישׁ רָ֥ץ לְבַדּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḏā·wiḏ yō·wō·šêḇ bên- šə·nê haš·šə·‘ā·rîm way·yê·leḵ haṣ·ṣō·p̄eh ’el- gaḡ haš·ša·‘ar ’el- ha·ḥō·w·māh way·yiś·śā ’eṯ- ‘ê·nāw way·yar wə·hin·nêh- ’îš rāṣ lə·ḇad·dōw
verses.literal: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall looked out - and saw . . . a man running alone . . .
verses.literalPt: Ora, Davi estava assentado entre as duas portas; a sentinela subiu ao eirado da porta acima da muralha, e levantou os olhos, e viu vir um homem correndo só.

verses.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א הַצֹּפֶה֙ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־ לְבַדּ֖וֹ בְּשׂוֹרָ֣ה בְּפִ֑יו וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ הָל֖וֹךְ וְקָרֵֽב׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·rā haṣ·ṣō·p̄eh way·yag·gêḏ lam·me·leḵ way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’im- lə·ḇad·dōw bə·śō·w·rāh bə·p̄îw way·yê·leḵ hā·lō·wḵ wə·qā·rêḇ
verses.literal: So he called out and told the king If he is alone . . . the king replied he bears good news As the first runner drew . . . near
verses.literalPt: Clamou a sentinela e deu a nova ao rei. O rei disse: Se ele vem só, traz notícias. O mensageiro aproximava-se cada vez mais.

verses.original: וַיַּ֣רְא הַצֹּפֶה֮ אִישׁ־ אַחֵ֣ר רָץ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֤א הַצֹּפֶה֙ אֶל־ הַשֹּׁעֵ֔ר וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־ אִ֖ישׁ רָ֣ץ לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ גַּם־ זֶ֥ה מְבַשֵּֽׂר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yar haṣ·ṣō·p̄eh ’îš- ’a·ḥêr rāṣ way·yiq·rā haṣ·ṣō·p̄eh ’el- haš·šō·‘êr way·yō·mer hin·nêh- ’îš rāṣ lə·ḇad·dōw way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ gam- zeh mə·ḇaś·śêr
verses.literal: the watchman saw another man running and he called out . . . to the gatekeeper Look Another man is running alone . . . This one also brings good news said the king
verses.literalPt: Viu a sentinela outro homem correndo, e clamou ao porteiro, e disse: Eis que vem outro homem correndo só. O rei disse: Este também traz notícias.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַצֹּפֶ֔ה אֲנִ֤י רֹאֶה֙ אֶת־ מְרוּצַ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן כִּמְרֻצַ֖ת אֲחִימַ֣עַץ בֶּן־ צָד֑וֹק וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אִֽישׁ־ ט֣וֹב זֶ֔ה וְאֶל־ בְּשׂוֹרָ֥ה טוֹבָ֖ה יָבֽוֹא׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer haṣ·ṣō·p̄eh ’ă·nî rō·’eh ’eṯ- mə·rū·ṣaṯ hā·ri·šō·wn kim·ru·ṣaṯ ’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ ben- ṣā·ḏō·wq way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’îš- ṭō·wḇ zeh wə·’el- bə·śō·w·rāh ṭō·w·ḇāh yā·ḇō·w
verses.literal: The watchman said The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok This is a good man said the king He comes with good news
verses.literalPt: Acrescentou a sentinela: Parece-me que o correr do primeiro é como o correr de Aimaás, filho de Zadoque. Disse o rei: Ele é homem de bem e trará boas-novas.

verses.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֲחִימַ֗עַץ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ שָׁל֔וֹם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לְאַפָּ֖יו אָ֑רְצָהס וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּרוּךְ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר סִגַּר֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ נָשְׂא֥וּ אֶת־ יָדָ֖ם בַּֽאדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·rā ’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ way·yō·mer ’el- ham·me·leḵ šā·lō·wm way·yiš·ta·ḥū lam·me·leḵ lə·’ap·pāw ʾå̄·rə·ṣå̄·hs way·yō·mer bā·rūḵ Yah·weh ’ĕ·lō·he·ḵā ’ă·šer sig·gar ’eṯ- hā·’ă·nā·šîm ’ă·šer- nā·śə·’ū ’eṯ- yā·ḏām ba·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king All is well And he bowed facedown . . . before the king He continued Blessed be the LORD your God He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king
verses.literalPt: Gritou Aimaás e disse ao rei: Paz! Prostrou-se com o rosto em terra perante o rei e disse: Bendito seja Jeová, teu Deus, que entregou os homens que levantaram a mão contra o rei, meu senhor!

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׁל֥וֹם לַנַּ֖עַר לְאַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחִימַ֡עַץ רָאִיתִי֩ הֶהָמ֨וֹן הַגָּד֜וֹל לִ֠שְׁלֹחַ אֶת־ עֶ֨בֶד הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ יוֹאָב֙ וְאֶת־ עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ וְלֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי מָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ šā·lō·wm lan·na·‘ar lə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm way·yō·mer ’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ rā·’î·ṯî he·hā·mō·wn hag·gā·ḏō·wl liš·lō·aḥ ’eṯ- ‘e·ḇeḏ ham·me·leḵ yō·w·’āḇ wə·’eṯ- ‘aḇ·de·ḵā wə·lō yā·ḏa‘·tî māh
verses.literal: The king asked Is the young man Absalom all right And Ahimaaz replied When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant I saw a great tumult but I do not know what it was
verses.literalPt: Perguntou o rei: Está bem o mancebo Absalão? Respondeu Aimaás: Quando Joabe enviou ao servo do rei, que sou eu, vi um grande alvoroço, porém não sei o que era.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ סֹ֖ב הִתְיַצֵּ֣ב כֹּ֑ה וַיִּסֹּ֖ב וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽד׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ sōḇ hiṯ·yaṣ·ṣêḇ kōh way·yis·sōḇ way·ya·‘ă·mōḏ
verses.literal: Move aside said the king and stand here So he stepped aside
verses.literalPt: Disse o rei: Põe-te ao lado e espera aqui. Ele se pôs ao lado e esperou de pé.

verses.original: וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכּוּשִׁ֖י בָּ֑א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַכּוּשִׁ֗י יִתְבַּשֵּׂר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־ שְׁפָטְךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם מִיַּ֖ד כָּל־ הַקָּמִ֥ים עָלֶֽיךָ׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·hin·nêh hak·kū·šî bā way·yō·mer hak·kū·šî yiṯ·baś·śêr ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ kî- šə·p̄ā·ṭə·ḵā Yah·weh hay·yō·wm mî·yaḏ kāl- haq·qā·mîm ‘ā·le·ḵā
verses.literal: Just then the Cushite came and said . . . May my lord the king . . . hear the good news Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you
verses.literalPt: Eis que chegou o cuxita e disse: Receba o rei, meu senhor, as novas. Hoje, Jeová te vingou de todos os que se levantaram contra ti.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ הַכּוּשִׁ֔י הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לַנַּ֖עַר לְאַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַכּוּשִׁ֗י יִהְי֤וּ כַנַּ֙עַר֙ אֹֽיְבֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ קָ֥מוּ עָלֶ֖יךָ לְרָעָֽה׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- hak·kū·šî hă·šā·lō·wm lan·na·‘ar lə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm way·yō·mer hak·kū·šî yih·yū ḵan·na·‘ar ’ō·yə·ḇê ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ wə·ḵōl ’ă·šer- qā·mū ‘ā·le·ḵā lə·rā·‘āh
verses.literal: The king . . . asked the Cushite Is the young man Absalom all right And the Cushite replied May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you to harm you be like that young man
verses.literalPt: O rei perguntou ao cuxita: Está bem o mancebo Absalão? Respondeu o cuxita: Como aquele mancebo o é, assim sejam os inimigos do rei, meu senhor, e todos os que se levantam contra ti para te fazerem o mal.

verses.original: וַיִּרְגַּ֣ז הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיַּ֛עַל עַל־ עֲלִיַּ֥ת הַשַּׁ֖עַר וַיֵּ֑בְךְּ וְכֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר בְּלֶכְתּ֗וֹ בְּנִ֤י אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ בְּנִ֣י בְנִ֣י אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֤ן מוּתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י תַחְתֶּ֔יךָ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּנִ֥י בְנִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yir·gaz ham·me·leḵ way·ya·‘al ‘al- ‘ă·lî·yaṯ haš·ša·‘ar way·yê·ḇək wə·ḵōh ’ā·mar bə·leḵ·tōw bə·nî ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm bə·nî ḇə·nî ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm mî- yit·tên mū·ṯî ’ă·nî ṯaḥ·te·ḵā ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm bə·nî ḇə·nî
verses.literal: The king was shaken and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept And as he walked he cried out O my son Absalom My son my son Absalom If only . . . I had died instead of you O Absalom my son my son
verses.literalPt: O rei ficou muito comovido, e subiu à sala que estava por cima da porta, e pôs-se a chorar; e, andando, dizia assim: Meu filho Absalão, meu filho, meu filho Absalão! Quem me dera que eu morrera por ti, Absalão, filho meu, filho meu!
